page.title: Best 3D Printer for ABS (2026): Heated-Chamber Picks That Stop Warping
page.desc: The best 3D printer for ABS has an actively heated chamber. We compare QIDI Q2, Plus5 and Max4 against Bambu P1S, Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 and Creality K2 Plus on chamber, nozzle and bed temperature.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 3D printer for ABS is the QIDI Q2 ({buy:qidi-q2}): a 65 °C actively heated chamber, a 370 °C nozzle and a 120 °C bed in a 270 × 270 × 256 mm enclosed CoreXY. The warping that ruins ABS comes from a cold chamber: the Bambu Lab P1S has no chamber heater and owners on Bambu's forum report 43 to 50 °C after a 30-minute heat soak, while the Q2 holds 65 °C under thermostat control. For parts over 10 inches, step up to the QIDI Plus5 ({buy:qidi-plus5}), which keeps the same 65 °C chamber on a 320 × 320 × 300 mm bed with a 550 W heater. If you want multi-color ABS with a mature filament system, the Bambu Lab P1S Combo is the better buy despite its passive chamber, because the QIDI Box jammed repeatedly in two independent reviews.

Prices and stock were read on QIDI's US store on 2026-11-06. All three QIDI printers are MET or ETL style enclosed machines with 3-stage filtration, which matters because ABS fumes are the second most common owner complaint after warping.
page.after:
What ABS owners complain about

Across Bambu's forum, Trustpilot, Tom's Hardware, Tom Sanladerer's review and owner-compiled issue lists, the same five problems repeat. Warping and corner lift on parts over about 7 inches came up most, almost always on printers without a chamber heater; Bambu P1S owners describe 30-minute heat soaks, 100 °C beds and glue to get close. Second is fumes: ABS smells, so buyers want an enclosure with a filter. Third, specific to QIDI, is PLA heat creep: six sources describe clogs when PLA is printed with the lid closed, and QIDI itself says keep the chamber at or below 45 °C for PLA. Fourth is the QIDI Box multi-color add-on, which jammed or failed to unload filament in three separate reviews. Fifth is noise: the Q2 measured 56 dB in one review, against about 48 dB for the Plus5 and 45 dB for the Centauri Carbon 2 in silent mode.

One safety note. The QIDI Plus 4, now discontinued, drew fire reports in late 2024 and 2025 tied to its chamber-heater relay. QIDI shipped replacement relays and the reviewer at 3DPrint.com withdrew his warning after several days of trouble-free printing. The Plus5 is a new design with a different 550 W heater; we have not seen an independent safety test of it, so budget for a smoke detector near any heated-chamber printer.

Which one by need

  • Mostly ABS or ASA, parts up to 10 inches, under $500: QIDI Q2 ({buy:qidi-q2}). It is the only printer at this price with a thermostat-controlled 65 °C chamber. Keep the stock slicer in its slower profile for cleaner overhangs.
  • Large ABS parts, helmets, enclosures: QIDI Plus5 ({buy:qidi-plus5}). Its 320 × 320 × 300 mm volume is 18 percent larger than the Plus 4 for the same price, and the 550 W heater reaches 65 °C faster. The Creality K2 Plus gives you 350 mm cubed and a 60 °C chamber if you need the extra 30 mm or Creality's CFS multi-color.
  • Biggest ABS parts under $1,100: QIDI Max4 ({buy:qidi-max4}), with a 390 × 390 × 340 mm heated chamber. Expect some firmware rough edges.
  • Multi-color ABS, polished software: Bambu Lab P1S Combo. Its AMS is far more reliable than the QIDI Box, and a 100 °C bed with a long heat soak handles ABS parts under about 7 inches. Expect to fight warping on bigger prints.
  • Mostly PLA, occasional ABS: Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 or Bambu P1S. A heated chamber works against PLA, and the Q2 needs its lid open for it.

Not recommended for ABS

Open-frame bed slingers such as the Bambu A1 and Creality Ender 3 series print ABS only with an aftermarket enclosure, and even then the chamber rarely passes 35 °C. The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 and Bambu P1S are good enclosed printers, but neither has a heater, so large ABS parts warp at the corners; two reviewers reported this on the original Centauri Carbon. The discontinued QIDI Plus 4 is still sold used; buy one only if the replacement relay has been fitted.
